ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPLICATION   NO. 3627 OF 2024  
Shubham Devendra Kumar .. Applicant
                  Versus
State of Maharashtra .. Respondent
....................
 Mr. Ayush Pasbola, Advocate through VC a/w. Ms. Mrunali Bhid e,
Advocates for Applicant.
 Ms. Mahalakshmi Ganapathy, APP for Respondent – State. 
......…...........
CORAM : MILIND N. JADHAV, J.
DATE : JANUARY 02, 2025.
P.C.:
1. Heard Mr. Pasbola, learned Advocate for Applicant through
VC and Ms. Ganapathy, learned APP for Respondent – State. 
2. Applicant before me is a first year Computer Engineering
Student of Lokmanya Tilak College of Engineering.  Complainant is
second year Engineering student in Vidyalankar Engineering Instit ute
at Wadala, Mumbai.  Both of them had joined private tuition c lasses
called “Rao Classes” in their Junior College days when they developed
affinity towards each  other which subsequently transformed into  a
relationship over a period of time. On 30.08.2024, they had a quarrel
and resultantly broke-off.  It is alleged that thereafter the  Complainant
circulated her objectionable photographs and sent emails and messages
to her relatives, College Principal and victim.
1 of 5

33.ABA.3627.24.doc
3. First  Information  Report  (for  short  “ FIR”)  is  thereafter
lodged  on  29.11.2024  and  in  the  FIR,  the  date  of  incident  f or
indictment of Applicant is stated from 30.08.2024. Indictment is on the
ground  that  in  order  to  defame  and  tarnish  the  image  of  the
Complainant,  the  Accused  repeatedly  sent  her  whatsapp  messages
leading the Complainant to block him; he repeatedly started sendi ng
emails from various emails; he sent her obscene emails als o and most
importantly it is alleged that he sent obscene messages and mo rphed
photographs to the email ids of the Complainant’s College Principal.  It
is further alleged that he sent Complainant’s photos and videos to her
mother and her friends. 
4. FIR is lodged under Section 78, 79, 356 (2) of the Bharat iya
Nyay Sanhita, 2023 (for short “
BNS”) and Section 66A and 67A of the
Information and Technology Act, 2000 (for short “IT Act”).
5. Mr. Pasbola, learned Advocate for Applicant would persuade
me to consider that  except Section 67A of the IT Act, rest of  the
offences are bailable. He would submit that Section 66A of the IT Act is
declared as unconstitutional. He would submit that the mobile phone
of the Applicant has been deposited with the Investigating Offi cer.  He
would  submit  that  he  would  extend  absolute  co-operation  to  the
Investigating Officer as desired. 
2 of 5

33.ABA.3627.24.doc
6. Ms. Ganapathy has vehemently contested this Anticipatory
Bail Application stating that custodial interrogation of the Ap plicant is
required in the present case for carrying out further investigation.  She
would submit the act of the Applicant circulating and dissemi nating
obscene photographs of the Complainant to her relatives and f riends
including her College Principal, is a very serious act and th erefore his
custodial interrogation is required.
7. Though the FIR states the date and duration of the incident
is on and from 30.08.2024, 
prima facie,  it is seen that Applicant and
Complainant knew each other from their Junior College days i.e.  the
years  preceding their  present  years  of  studying  in  the  Engineering
Collage.
8. What the learned Prosecutor has stated can be investigated
and recovered by the Investigating Officer from the relatives o f the
Complainant,  from  her  friends  and  from  her  College Principal,  for
which in my opinion custodial interrogation of the Applicant w ill not
be necessary.  
9. In view of the above, Applicant is directed to hand over his
laptop, I-pad and computer from which emails were sent by th em and
received by the aforementioned parties. 
10. Anticipatory  Bail  Application  stands  allowed  in  terms  of
prayer clause (a). 
3 of 5

33.ABA.3627.24.doc
11. In view of the facts of the case, interim protection is gr anted
on the following terms and conditions:-
(i) In the event of the arrest, Applicant be enlarged on bai l
on executing P.R. Bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- with
one or two sureties in the like amount;
(ii) Applicant shall report to the Investigating Officer of t he
concerned Police Station everyday from 13.01.2025 to
16.01.2025 from 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 noon in the first
instance and thereafter as and when called for by the
Investigating  Officer  alongwith  the  requisite
information / documents; 
(iii) Applicant shall furnish particulars of his address and
mobile number to the Investigating Officer within two
days from today;
(iv) Applicant shall not misuse his liberty in any manner or
influence  the  informant,  witnesses  or  any  person
concerned with the case and he shall not tamper with
the evidence;
(v)  It  is  directed  that  Applicant  shall  extend  complete
cooperate in the investigation of the instant case;
4 of 5

33.ABA.3627.24.doc
(vi) Applicant shall not make any attempts to re-associate
with the victim  girl in any manner either through a
device or in-person; and
(vii) Any infraction of the conditions shall entail revocatio n
of this order. 
12. Parties to act on a server copy of this order. 
13. Anticipatory Bail Application is disposed. 
                                  [ MILIND N. JADHAV, J. ]
